week_focus: Prioritized trading-agent upgrades: Claude skills, financial MCP servers, backtesting engines, and dashboard charting infrastructure.

findings.name: tradermonty/claude-trading-skills
findings.description: A Claude Code skills repository focused on equity investors and traders, with workflows for market analysis, technical charting, economic calendars, and trading strategy development. It appears directly aligned with Claude Code's SKILL.md pattern and is the closest match to an installable trading skill pack.
findings.relevance: This is directly useful for JCF HQ because Crisp, Blade, and Oracle can borrow structured workflows for backtesting, signal generation, and market-data reasoning instead of relying on loose prompts.

findings.name: Alpaca MCP Server
findings.description: Alpaca's MCP server connects AI assistants to Alpaca's trading and market-data APIs. It supports natural-language research, account inspection, market analysis, and order workflows through a structured MCP interface.
findings.relevance: This matters for JCF HQ because it could give Crisp a cleaner bridge into equities, crypto, options, and paper/live execution workflows while keeping tool calls auditable.

findings.name: EODHD Financial Data MCP Server
findings.description: EODHD provides an MCP server for real-time and historical financial data, including equities, fundamentals, technical analysis, and macroeconomic indicators. It exposes financial API documentation as MCP resources, making it easier for agents to discover available data safely.
findings.relevance: This could strengthen Oracle and long-term stock research by giving agents structured access to fundamentals, macro context, and historical market data without custom scraping.

findings.name: Financial Datasets MCP Server
findings.description: Financial Datasets offers an MCP server for real-time financial data such as stock prices, financial statements, SEC filings, and news. The server is designed for AI assistants that need structured company and market context.
findings.relevance: This is useful for JCF HQ's research layer because Oracle can use filings, earnings, and news context to validate market theses before surfacing opportunities.

findings.name: NautilusTrader
findings.description: NautilusTrader is a high-performance open-source trading engine for backtesting and live algorithmic strategies. Its Rust core with Python integration focuses on deterministic execution, event-driven design, and research-to-live parity.
findings.relevance: This is a serious candidate for upgrading Crisp or Blade's backtesting layer because it is built for production-grade strategy validation, not just notebook experiments.

findings.name: OpenBB
findings.description: OpenBB is an open-source investment research platform with Python-first access to equities, crypto, macro, derivatives, and alternative data. It is designed for extensible financial analysis and automation.
findings.relevance: JCF HQ could use OpenBB as a research backend for Oracle and dashboard enrichment, especially for cross-asset context and repeatable market scans.

findings.name: Claude Code Agent Teams
findings.description: Agent Teams is Anthropic's Claude Code orchestration feature for coordinating multiple agents with separate context windows, dependencies, and direct teammate communication. It is built for larger coding and research tasks where parallel specialists improve throughput.
findings.relevance: This maps cleanly onto JCF HQ's Huncho-to-sub-agent structure and could improve how Crisp, Blade, Oracle, and dashboard agents coordinate without dumping all context into one thread.

findings.name: MCP Registry Preview
findings.description: The official MCP Registry is an open catalog and API for discovering public MCP servers. It standardizes server metadata and gives developers a central place to find, evaluate, and integrate MCP tools.
findings.relevance: This should become part of Lucy's weekly scout workflow because it can surface new financial, browser, database, and automation MCP servers before they hit mainstream lists.

findings.name: TradingView Lightweight Charts
findings.description: TradingView Lightweight Charts is an open-source charting library optimized for financial time-series visualization. It supports candlesticks, line charts, histograms, responsive layouts, and high-performance rendering.
findings.relevance: This is a strong fit for JCF HQ dashboards because Crisp, Blade, and Oracle outputs can be rendered as fast, readable market panels without heavy charting dependencies.

findings.name: Langfuse
findings.description: Langfuse is an open-source LLM observability platform for tracing agent runs, prompts, tool calls, evaluations, and costs. It helps teams inspect where agents fail, drift, or spend too much.
findings.relevance: This could give JCF HQ better visibility into trading-agent decisions, weekly scout runs, and model spend, which matters if agents are operating on schedules or touching financial workflows.

summary: This week's strongest signal is that trading-focused Claude Code skills and financial MCP servers are maturing fast enough to be useful for JCF HQ now. The best immediate win is tradermonty/claude-trading-skills because it is closest to a direct installable skill pack and matches the way Huncho already coordinates specialist agents. Alpaca, EODHD, and Financial Datasets are the strongest MCP/API candidates for structured market data and execution workflows. For infrastructure, Claude Agent Teams and Langfuse are worth tracking because they improve coordination, traceability, and reliability across the agent roster.
